findings.name: Lifetime exhaustion detaches input failure handling while accepted requests still run

source_lines.reason: overflow sets exhausted and calls detachInput while leaving state OPEN
detachInput removes end, close and error listeners as well as parser/data listener
transport failure should finish immediately, but the OPEN pump dispatches the queued request if no failure is observed

reproduction.case: maxLifetimeRequests=2, hold dispatch(1), queue request 2, send extra request 3 to trigger exhaustion; end/destroy/error the input, then resolve dispatch 1
reproduction.expected: transport closure observed immediately, late active result discarded, queued request 2 never dispatched
reproduction.actual: all three exhausted cases closedBeforeCompletion=false, dispatchIds=[1,2], responseIds=[1,2], onError reports only limit/-32084
reproduction.controls: same end/error/close cases without exhaustion closed immediately, dispatchIds=[1], no response writes

findings.impact: A disconnected/failed input can start queued work that the transport contract requires discarding. A never-settling active dispatch can also leave this exhausted server open until the host explicitly closes it; this latter consequence is static inference, not an executed indefinite-hang test.
findings.recommended_action: Separate stopping frame admission from input end/error/close observation. Retain failure listeners through accepted-work drain, with terminal cleanup on I/O loss. Preserve the passing slow-drain and explicit-close tests and add this regression matrix.
